oncall-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT PAGE — spike in 5xxs from eu-canary (~03:02 UTC). Pager: Sanjay P.
Sanjay P.: I'm on it. seeing 502/503 across a subset of inference-runtime pods in eu-west-1 canary tier. dashboards -> error rate 7.9% for canary-routes, prod baseline 0.2%.
Carla M.: any recent deploys or flag changes?
Sanjay P.: Canary got a small autoscaler change and a GPU scheduling tweak in the last deploy (commit 7b9f2c1). I can see pod restarts correlated with higher token length requests.
Alex B.: If scheduling is misplacing pods on packed nodes that could increase OOM/kills -> 5xx. We should kill the feature flag for the new scheduler and revert the single commit if needed.
Sanjay P.: Agreed. Killing flag first to stop new routing: `redwoodctl feature set scheduler/new-placement false --env eu-canary`
ops-bot: Feature flag `scheduler/new-placement` set to `false` in eu-canary by Alex B. (via redwoodctl). :white_check_mark:
Sanjay P.: flag flip reduced errors from 7.9% -> 2.1% in 90s. Still above baseline but trending down.
Carla M.: Prepare a quick revert of 7b9f2c1 as a single-commit rollback. Who can cut the patch? We want minimal change.
Alex B.: I got it. Reverting locally: `git revert --no-edit 7b9f2c1` -> open PR `hotfix/revert-scheduler-7b9f2c1` -> CI -> release.
Sanjay P.: I'll keep the canary pinned to prior runtime for traffic split while build runs.
Alex B.: CI passed. Cutting release: `deploy-tool release --env eu-canary --commit HEAD --strategy canary --notes "revert scheduler placement"`
ops-bot: Deploy started for hotfix/revert-scheduler-7b9f2c1 to eu-canary. Rollout watching.
Sanjay P.: Rolling updates completed on 3/4 canary pods, error rate down to 0.3% after full canary rollout.
Carla M.: Good. Any customer impact to report? Which customers hit errors?
Sanjay P.: Correlated with high-token sessions from two enterprise customers (acme-analytics and glyph.ai), about 0.7% of total requests. No data loss, only transient 5xx on generation endpoints.
Alex B.: Sending note to CS to preempt with brief incident advisory. No PII exposed.
Jordan L.: I'm taking follow-up on-call for the morning. Leaving runbook: verify canary metrics at 10m/1h, unpin if stable, escalate if >1% sustained.
Sanjay P.: Handoff acked. Root cause hypothesis: the scheduler tweak interacted poorly with node packing + long-seq requests causing GPU memory pressure -> transient 5xx.
Carla M.: Postmortem action items: (1) add canary perf tests with long-seq traffic; (2) add predeploy canary memory pressure simulation; (3) tighten alert thresholds for canary >1% 5xx.
oncall-bot: Incident marked RESOLVED — mitigations applied (flag kill, single-commit revert), monitoring stable. Final status: no customer-facing outage after hotfix. :white_check_mark:
Alex B.: Thanks everyone for fast coordination. I'll open the follow-up PRs for tests and alert tuning.
Jordan L.: Leaving a summary in #incidents-postmortems later today.
Sanjay P.: closing thread, will attach timelines and logs in the postmortem. :thumbsup:
